Tessa / Ben —

High-level thoughts from pricing: we can support a 60-day price hold for the committed SKU mix provided the customer locks the primary SKU split (A100-80 vs A100-40 etc.) and signs a standard reserve SOW. Operational risk: if our underlying procurement costs spike >20% vs baseline for the tranche month, we may need a contractual pass-through or credit mechanism — otherwise our margin erodes quickly.

Suggested structure (fast to approve):
- Standard 12-month reserved commitment at X% discount vs list (fill numbers in with finance).
- 60-day price hold from signature confirming SKU split.
- GPU-price-swing clause: if our monthly cost index (internal procurement index) increases >15% vs baseline for two consecutive weeks, customer is eligible for a one-time credit equal to 50% of the incremental cost above the 15% threshold (to a cap of 10% of the total committed value).
- Exec approval required for credit >10% of committed value.

I’ll need finance to quantify the typical exposure for a 120K-hour deal across a reasonable volatility band. Ben, can you run a quick pro-forma with +/- 10/15/25% GPU cost shocks?

-Karthik

Looping in the pro-forma (attached) — ran three scenarios (+10%, +15%, +25% wholesale GPU cost). Key outputs:

- +10%: incremental cost exposure ~ $42k over 12 mo; one-time credit at 50% -> $21k (0.8% of committed value)
- +15%: exposure ~ $63k; credit -> $31.5k (1.2% of committed value)
- +25%: exposure ~ $105k; credit -> $52.5k (2.0% of committed value)

Recommendation: offer the 60-day hold + the 15% threshold with a 50% shared-credit up to a 2.5% committed-value cap. That keeps the max payout predictable and within margin guardrails. If the customer pushes for lower threshold, we should require an increased customer commitment (longer tenor or higher minimums).

Also propose an operational fallback: if capacity tightness forces us to allocate across customers, Neurolytics gets priority up to 90% of the committed rate for the first 6 months (subject to force majeure and region constraints). That’s a trade we can offer to secure the deal.

I’ll attach the CSV (pro_forma_capacity_table.csv) with the numbers.

—Ben
